segments.speaker: KASLIWAL
segments.text: 48, The CHAIRMAN pointed out to the Soviet Union representative that the document in question was not an official United Nations document and had never been circulated as one,

segments.speaker: DOUGLAS GLOVER
segments.text: 49, Sir Douglas GLOVER (United Kingdom) said that as the voting was not yet finished, the USSR representative's remarks were a wholly unwarranted breach of the rules of procedure,

segments.speaker: KASLIWAL
segments.text: 50. The CHAIRMAN invited the Committee to continue the voting, and called for a vote on article 3.

segments.speaker: KASLIWAL
segments.text: 51, The CHAIRMAN called for a vote on article 4,

segments.speaker: IDRIS
segments.text: 52, Mr. IDRIS (Indonesia) requested a separate vote on the words "only in sofarasthis may be compatible with the nature of these rights",
The retention of those words was approved by 72 votes to one, with 13 abstentions.

segments.speaker: KASLIWAL
segments.text: 53. The CHAIPMAN put to the vote article 4 asa whole,
Article 4 as a whole was adopted unanimously.

segments.speaker: KASLIWAL
segments.text: 54, The CHAIRMAN put article 5 to the vote.
Adoption of articles 3 and 5 of the draft Covenant on Civil and Political Rights

segments.speaker: KASLIWAL
segments.text: 55. The CHAIRMAN proposed that the Committee should vote on articles 3 and 5 of the draft Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (E/2573, annex 1B), the text of which corresponded to that of articles 3 and 5 of the draft Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights.
